teaching_carrier.ordinary_lowercase: Source a–s map in alphabetic order to the first19 signs in ordinary_signs; t–z map to q followed by the first7 ordinary signs. This is one general letter table, never a word table.
teaching_carrier.rare_character_rule: For zero-based index j in rare_characters_in_order, write y followed by rare_selectors[floor(j/8)] and rare_selectors[j mod 8]. All three marks are consumed as one source character. Unlisted source characters are outside this teaching edition and cause an explicit failure, never deletion or guessed replacement.
teaching_carrier.marker: r never occurs in the letter carrier and is reserved for the mechanism declared in this card.
teaching_carrier.source_contract: Inputs are nonempty source tokens separated by single spaces, with explicit paragraph breaks. Uppercase, listed punctuation and digits are retained by the rare-character table. Repeated whitespace and exact physical source lineation are outside the declared input contract; semantic words, word order and paragraph boundaries are retained. No lowercasing, grammatical normalization or expansion of ambiguous historical spelling is performed.
teaching_carrier.reader_cost: The learner must know the source language, its ordinary spellings, the26 lowercase entries and the entire listed rare-character table, plus the mechanism-specific table/rules. Rare-character escape can be slow and long; its cost is charged. Drawings are already familiar transcription-designated shapes, but their artificial assignment is not a native letter or word-value claim.
teaching_carrier.decoding: Parse ordinary single signs, q plus exactly one permitted letter selector, or y plus exactly two rare selectors; reject unused combinations. The distinct marker r cannot be confused with a spelled source character. Multi-letter transcription labels such as ch name one working drawing here, without claiming that native writing has independently established these atoms.

title: RAW UNREVIEWED: ordinary full spelling with a fixed compulsory literal-multigraph shorthand
summary: A human copies ordinary meaningful source words through one alphabet, replacing a fixed list of exact spelling substrings by explicit two-sign shortcuts. Unknown words are written by the identical rule. The expansion table contains literal substrings, not freely assigned meanings or whole-message identifiers.

design.purpose: Reduce repeated spelling effort while preserving exact lexical order, spelling, negation, comparisons and references without a semantic-root vocabulary.
encode: At each character position within one source token, find every listed exact case-sensitive substring beginning there. If any exists, take the longest and write r followed by its fixed selector; advance by the whole matched substring. Otherwise encode exactly one source character with the shared carrier and advance one position.

Do not choose a shorter match, decline a shortcut, match across a source space, or add a new shortcut for a difficult message. The listed16 entries have no equal-length duplicate spelling, so longest-match ties cannot arise.
Preserve one visible group per source token. Wrap only between complete groups; line position never changes the rule.
decode: Inside each visible group, r followed by one of the16 selectors expands to that exact substring; every other unit follows the ordinary carrier.
After decoding, re-encode with the unchanged longest-match rule; a noncanonical spelling is rejected, even if expansion would produce readable text. A final r or unsupported selector is malformed.
design.single_new_and_repeat: One source character is fully spelled. Unfamiliar words use the same fixed scan with no dictionary search or exception marker. Repeated characters are kept unless they participate in one of the exact declared substrings. Consecutive identical words produce identical complete groups written twice.
design.constructive_example: At the abstract instruction level, lowercase 'einen' must use the single shortcut for 'einen'; the encoding shortcut('ein')+spell('en') is noncanonical. 'schmal' uses shortcut('sch') followed by the complete spelling of 'mal'. These are invented teaching examples, not Voynich readings.
design.learning_cost: The common alphabet and rare-character table plus16 exact substring-to-selector entries and one greedy rule. Source-language vocabulary and spelling are still assumed. The list's choice is an overt design cost, not an empirical result.
design.necessary_observable_difference: With this list and key fixed, every occurrence of a listed substring at the current scan position forces the same shortcut and source-word boundaries survive. Optional free spelling of the same substring is forbidden. Pure letter renaming has no such longest-match canonicality requirement.
design.smallest_falsifier: A blind human round-trip on a short externally chosen ordinary message containing overlaps and an unfamiliar word must reconstruct every spelling with only the printed tables. One ambiguous expansion, dropped distinction or inability to reject the 'ein'+'en' representation of 'einen' fails this exact lesson. For a later native conjunction, any required noncanonical representation under the frozen source/key falsifies that conjunction.
design.strongest_counterexample: IDEA933 already shows that canonical shortcut coverage can be vacuous under a free source/key: unused literal values can make every observed string legal. This card supplies a fixed source spelling lesson, but cannot identify a native key merely by output coverage. Its16 selected entries also favor German orthography and may cost more to learn or write than they save.
design.statistical_limit: Visible word frequency and type counts are identical to the source tokens because encoding is injective per token and preserves spaces. This mechanism alone cannot fix a source's incompatible whole-word frequency distribution; only spelling-level structure changes.

predecessors_and_limits.relation: Same broad compulsory-substring family. Difference is a fully frozen ordinary-language forward lesson and overt learning costs, not a new solution to933's native source-free key nonidentifiability. Its failure is retained.
Related contraction proposal; this exact spelling transducer does not reconstruct unspoken case endings or assume ending preservation.
The earlier shell atlas assumed supplied whole-card names and was not a manuscript spelling decoder. Its later468/469/519 wrappers do not supply native meanings for this alphabet.
